findings.text: Two build variants exist for tree and cursor diagnostics. One variant maintains global run and pass counts and on failure emits contextual dumps plus a stack trace, with warn forms also yielding a boolean outcome. The other variant forwards directly to generic bug and warn facilities.

Cursor range update warns when the cursor is active yet the requested start lies outside its current bounds, then records the new start and end. A resetting wrapper clears cursor state before applying the range, and a single position helper expresses a degenerate range where both ends coincide.

Whether a tree uses external synchronization is decided by masked flag bits. Initialization stores supplied flags, prepares embedded spin protection only for internally locked trees, and publishes an empty root through an ordered RCU store. Default initialization supplies cleared flags.

RCU usage and height are encoded in flag bits with dedicated readers. Enabling or disabling RCU mode returns early when already in the desired state; otherwise it updates the flag while asserting that an external lock is held, or while briefly acquiring and releasing the internal lock.
A traversal helper repeatedly looks up successive entries within an index interval, starting with an initial search and continuing with an after-position search until no entry remains.
Upward and downward alignment helpers assume the alignment is a power of two and derive a mask from one less than that value, preserving the input type for the mask.

Additional helpers support arbitrary alignments through quotient and remainder arithmetic, plus several divide-and-round forms for upward, closest, and power-of-two cases, including sector sized variants that select width appropriate division.

A fractional multiply helper reduces overflow by combining quotient and remainder contributions. Sector division aliases the generic 64-bit division helper. A scaling helper maps a 32-bit value into a half open range using wide intermediate precision, and a 64-bit root helper narrows the generic root result.

Absolute value selection dispatches on the static type among narrow to wide signed and unsigned forms, converting unsigned inputs to signed first and treating character data as signed while preserving its result type. A difference helper enforces identical operand types and returns the non negative distance by subtracting the smaller from the larger.

Paired numerator and denominator records are provided for several integer widths, generated from a common template and instantiated for unsigned bytes and for signed and unsigned sixteen and thirty two bit forms.

Sixty four bit division helpers cover unsigned and signed dividends with narrow or wide divisors, returning the quotient while storing the remainder through an out parameter. Simpler wrappers discard the remainder, and long named aliases select signed or unsigned wide division according to configuration.

Widening multiply, add, multiply then shift, signed magnitude handling, and multiply then divide helpers support fixed point arithmetic with both wide integer and decomposed word implementations, alongside round up and closest division macros and a 64-bit round up to multiple helper.

A heap header tracks current occupancy and capacity together with a data pointer and embedded storage for the preallocated case. A character specialization and a zero capacity definition macro allow generic reuse, while a callback record supplies ordering and exchange hooks with opaque context.

Initialization clears occupancy, records capacity, and selects caller supplied storage when present else the embedded area. Peeking yields the base element or null when empty, and fullness compares occupancy against capacity. Thin wrappers adapt typed heaps through container conversion.

Downward restoration follows the smaller child path to a leaf, including handling of an unpaired final leaf, then backtracks to the ordered slot and shifts entries along the path. Upward restoration moves a newly placed element toward the root while ordering against its parent fails. Index translation between scaled offsets and logical positions accounts for element size alignment.

Alignment detection considers size and, where unaligned access is costly, base address. Swap routine selection prefers the widest safe transfer, and a dispatcher invokes the chosen word or byte mover or a caller custom hook. Movers exchange elements from the end toward the start with width specific handling.
Three swap selector identities are encoded as small distinctive pointer values to distinguish optimized movers from genuine function addresses.
Several helpers have external linkage and serve as callable entry points for range setup, word and byte exchange, swap selection and dispatch, and heap lifecycle and restoration.

Absolute value of the most negative signed input lacks a representable positive result and is documented as undefined. Division and modulus helpers assume a non zero divisor. Power of two rounding requires power of two alignment, and generic rounding assumes compatible types that avoid truncation.

Heap restoration dereferences the ordering hook and assumes non zero element size with occupancy consistent with capacity. Swap selection and parent computation assume sizes whose low bit structure supports the masking arithmetic.
